title: Monotonicity-Constrained Chirped Stack with Cumulative Exponential Mapping
scientific_hypothesis: Enforcing monotonic thickness progression via cumulative exponential parameterization (t_i = t_base + Σ exp(ξ_j)) will reduce optimizer degrees of freedom, smooth the loss landscape, and improve convergence compared to unconstrained chirped optimization, while maintaining the depth-graded principle for broadened UV reflection band.
design_principle: Chirped distributed Bragg reflector with monotonically increasing optical thickness from air to substrate to broaden the UV reflection band (300-450 nm) while maintaining SWIR transmission (1000-1700 nm) through reduced index contrast at longer wavelengths.
proposed_topology: 30-layer chirped stack: Air | [HfO2/SiO2]_15 | Fused Silica substrate. Layer sequence starts with HfO2 at air interface, alternates HfO2/SiO2, ends with SiO2 at substrate interface for environmental durability.
design_variables: 15 cumulative exponential thickness parameters (ξ_j) for bilayer pairs
soft_objectives: Maximize average transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band
Maximize average reflectance in 300-450 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: Outermost SiO2 layer >= 200 nm for environmental durability per evidence
theory_basis: Chirped DBR theory for bandwidth broadening
Cumulative exponential mapping for monotonicity enforcement
expected_advantages: Smoother optimization landscape due to reduced effective DOF
Maintains route_02's chirped principle while addressing numerical convergence issues
known_risks: Monotonicity constraint may limit optimal solutions if non-monotonic thickness profile is actually superior
Cumulative parameterization may introduce numerical stiffness if ξ_j values span large ranges
execution_request_english: Optimize a 30-layer HfO2/SiO2 chirped multilayer coating on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: HfO2(1)/SiO2(2)/HfO2(3)/SiO2(4)/HfO2(5)/SiO2(6)/HfO2(7)/SiO2(8)/HfO2(9)/SiO2(10)/HfO2(11)/SiO2(12)/HfO2(13)/SiO2(14)/HfO2(15)/SiO2(16)/HfO2(17)/SiO2(18)/HfO2(19)/SiO2(20)/HfO2(21)/SiO2(22)/HfO2(23)/SiO2(24)/HfO2(25)/SiO2(26)/HfO2(27)/SiO2(28)/HfO2(29)/SiO2(30). Implement monotonicity-enforcing parameterization: define each layer thickness t_i = t_base + cumulative_sum(exp(ξ_j)) for j=0 to i, where ξ_j are the optimizable parameters and t_base is a fixed offset. Evaluate at normal incidence, unpolarized illumination. Optimize for maximum transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band and maximum reflectance in 300-450 nm band. Constrain outermost SiO2 layer (layer 30) thickness >= 200 nm for environmental durability. Use gradient-based optimizer with the monotonicity mapping to reduce effective degrees of freedom. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 300-450 nm, 1000-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmission in 1000-1700 nm; high reflection in 300-450 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: low transmission in 300-450 nm; low reflection in 1000-1700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count <= 30; materials restricted to HfO2 and SiO2.
revision_reason: Direct refinement of route_02 implementing feedback directive: monotonicity-enforcing variable mapping via cumulative exponential parameterization to constrain optimizer to physically required air-to-substrate increasing regime, reduce effective DOF, and smooth loss landscape for faster gradient descent convergence.
